title: Kurt Schwitters, Anna Blume. Dichtungen, 1919 (cover)
lede: Schwitters’s first book of poems has a cover he drew himself: script, letter-spaced capitals, a scattered drawing, and four large red letters that spell dada.
summary: Pen drawing of a face, wheel, and windmill, script and capitals in black, and big red lowercase d a d a. Kurt Schwitters, Hannover, 1919.

source.label: Wikimedia Commons: Kurt Schwitters, Anna Blume. Dichtungen, 1919, first edition

evidence.note: Inspected the Commons photograph of a first-edition copy offered on ZVAB ([Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kurt_Schwitters_-_Anna_Blume._Dichtungen,_1919.jpg), 843 × 1302 px original; the stored 960 px Commons thumbnail is slightly upscaled). The copy is a dealer’s copy; its owner is not known.

styles.note: A Dada book cover: red letters spelling dada break through a scattered black drawing, and script, capitals, and roman letters mix. Partial fit: it is drawn by hand, not set from type or photographs.

context: Commons records the image as *Anna Blume. Dichtungen*, Paul Steegemann Verlag, Hannover, 1919, first edition, in the series Die Silbergäule, volumes 39–40, tagged PD-Art (PD-old-auto-1923, death year 1948). [Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kurt_Schwitters_-_Anna_Blume._Dichtungen,_1919.jpg).

Wikipedia says that the publication of the poem “An Anna Blume” in August 1919, with his first one-man show at Der Sturm, made Schwitters a well-known artist by the end of that year. [Wikipedia: Kurt Schwitters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Schwitters). He later printed it again in [Merz 1](ref:schwitters-merz-1-holland-dada-1923).
observed: The cover is printed in black and red on grey-green paper.
The series title “Die Silbergäule.” is in a large German script at the top, underlined.
“A-N-N-A” is letter-spaced in thin capitals with hyphens. “ANNA BLUME.” is in thin roman capitals in the lower third, and “Kurt Schwitters.” and “Dichtungen.” are in script, each underlined.
Four large red lowercase serif letters, “d a d a”, climb diagonally across the middle from lower left to upper right.
A loose pen drawing fills the middle: a face in profile, a large wheel, a windmill, a small figure, a heart, a cart, arrows, and small crosses, signed “Schwitters 1919”.
The publisher’s line “Paul Steegemann, Verlag, Hannover.” is in script at the bottom.
interpretation: The red “dada” letters do the same job as the giant red letters on [the 1922 soirée program](ref:van-doesburg-schwitters-kleine-dada-soiree-1922): one word in the accent color cuts across everything else. The rest of the cover is closer to expressionist drawing.
borrow: Run one word in large red letters diagonally across a black drawing, so the accent sets the direction.
Mix script, letter-spaced capitals, and roman capitals for title, author, and series.

images.alt: Grey-green book cover with a black pen drawing of a face, a wheel, a windmill, and arrows, the words Die Silbergäule and Kurt Schwitters in script, ANNA BLUME in thin capitals, and four large red letters d a d a climbing diagonally across the middle.
images.caption: Kurt Schwitters, cover of *Anna Blume. Dichtungen*, Paul Steegemann Verlag, Hannover, 1919. Dealer’s copy, image via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kurt_Schwitters_-_Anna_Blume._Dichtungen,_1919.jpg), PD-Art.

rights.statement: Commons tags the image PD-Art (PD-old-auto-1923, death year 1948). Schwitters, a German author, signed the cover drawing and died in 1948, so the cover is public domain in Germany. It was published in 1919, so it is public domain in the United States. The photograph is a plain record of a flat cover.
